q: What is the negation of: “Some phones are cheap”?
steps: Negation must be true exactly when the original is false.
“All are” negates to “Some are not”; “Some are” negates to “None are” — and vice versa.

traps.why: The negation of "All are X" is "Some are not X" — NOT "None are X" (both could be false at once).
Check: could this and the original both be true? A real negation can never share a truth value with the original.

q: Is this argument valid? “If it rains, the game is canceled. The game is canceled. Therefore it rained.”
steps: This is the form “affirming the consequent”.
It is a classic fallacy — the game could be canceled (or on) for other reasons; the conditional only promises one direction.

traps.why: Valid forms: affirm the IF-part (modus ponens) or deny the THEN-part (modus tollens). Affirming the then-part or denying the if-part proves nothing.

traps.ans: Valid only if it actually rained
traps.why: Validity is about FORM, not facts — a valid argument guarantees the conclusion whenever the premises hold, regardless of the weather.

q: In a class, 30 students take math, 18 take biology, and 5 take both. How many take math or biology (or both)?
steps: \(30 + 18 - 5 = 43\) — subtracting the overlap so nobody is counted twice.

The overlap is SUBTRACTED, not added: those students already appear in both counts.

q: A gym charges a \$30 joining fee plus \$5 per visit. Write the cost model and find the cost of 8 visits.
steps: Per-visit charge is the slope; the joining fee is the fixed (starting) value: \(C(x) = 5x + 30\).

traps.why: Slope and intercept swapped — the per-visit rate multiplies x; the one-time fee stands alone.
The joining fee applies once but it still applies — add it to the visit charges.

q: A phone plan's cost is modeled by \(C(g) = 25g + 100\), where \(g\) is gigabytes used. What does the 25 represent?
steps: In \(y = mx + b\), the slope \(m\) is the rate of change — cost per unit of \(g\).
Here: \$25 per additional gigabyte. (The \$100 is the fixed base charge.)

traps.why: The base charge is the intercept 100 (the cost at g = 0). The coefficient on g is the per-gigabyte rate.
The total depends on usage: C(g). The 25 is a RATE, dollars per gigabyte.

q: Using the model \(C(x) = 20x + 100\), for what \(x\) is the cost exactly \$220?
steps: Set the model equal to the target: \(20x + 100 = 220\).

traps.why: Subtract the fixed 100 BEFORE dividing by the rate — only the variable part scales with x.
After subtracting 100, still divide by the per-unit rate 20.
